lyrics:
[Intro: solo piano and voice, slow and free]
I had a radio beside my bed
A yellow dial, a wire for a thread
And every night a voice I never met
Played me songs I can't forget
But one cold morning, turning it on
There was a hiss where the voice had gone
I stood there with my toast gone cold
Eleven years, and feeling old
The day the dial went dark

[Chorus: tempo doubles, acoustic guitar, crowd singing]
So long, so long, to the Saturday song
The needle's off the record and the DJ's gone
We sang it in the car park with the windows down
The last ones in a one-song town
Who's going to play it again?

[Verse 1: brisk folk-rock, piano and drums]
Now the first one that I ever bought
Was a boy with a quiff and a voice like a shot
My mother said "turn that down" and danced
Behind the door when she thought I'd glanced
Then came the summer of the flowered vans
The fuzzy guitars and the tambourine hands
And we thought the world would turn on a tune
We were twelve, and it was June

[Chorus: crowd singing, handclaps]
So long, so long, to the Saturday song
The needle's off the record and the DJ's gone
We sang it in the car park with the windows down
The last ones in a one-song town
Who's going to play it again?

[Verse 2: brisk, band fuller]
Then the mirror balls and the platform shoes
The safety pins and the three-chord news
A robot sang and a drum machine
Turned every colour into green
And the big hair came and the big hair went
And a kid in flannel said what he meant
Then a box no bigger than a pack of cards
Held every song, and somehow none were ours

[Chorus: crowd singing, handclaps]
So long, so long, to the Saturday song
The needle's off the record and the DJ's gone
We sang it in the car park with the windows down
The last ones in a one-song town
Who's going to play it again?

[Verse 3: slow again, piano and voice only]
Now I've got it all in a pane of glass
Every song there ever was, first to last
It knows what I like before I do
It never plays me something new
So I went to the attic for the yellow dial
Blew the dust off, sat a while
And through the hiss, so faint and far
Somebody, somewhere, playing guitar

[Final Chorus: slow, then the crowd joins, building]
So hello, hello, to the Saturday song
The needle's on the record, it was there all along
We'll sing it in the car park with the windows down
The first ones in a one-song town
We're going to play it again
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: A slow, free opening at about 72 BPM, then a brisk folk-rock 138 BPM for the body of the song, and a slow final verse. G major. Storytelling that keeps turning into a singalong.

VOICE: Male tenor, clear, bright and sincere, in a folk style with every word audible. He sings the slow sections alone. The choruses are sung by a crowd in a room, loosely and happily, as if at closing time.

INSTRUMENTS: Piano, played simply at first and then with a rolling, barrelhouse energy. Strummed acoustic guitar. A walking bass. A drum kit that enters with the first chorus. Handclaps. A little electric guitar. Radio static at the start and end.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, voice and piano, slow, nine lines. 0:55 Chorus 1, the tempo doubles and the crowd comes in. 1:20 Verse 1. 1:50 Chorus 2. 2:15 Verse 2. 2:45 Chorus 3. 3:10 Verse 3, slow again, piano and voice. 4:05 Final chorus, starting slowly with one voice, the crowd joining and the tempo picking up, ending on a held chord at 4:55.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1970s folk-rock: natural, warm and live, piano and voice close, the crowd roomy and unpolished.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The jump in tempo into the first chorus at 0:55.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The loss is not a plane crash but the end of listening together. The third verse is about an algorithm that never plays anything new, and the ending is hopeful: he finds the old radio and someone is still out there playing.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Loss, a tour of memory, weariness, rediscovery.
